title: QuantTask input v1
description: Domain input payload for the Quant adapter's normalize_task. Carries the study identity plus the quantitative-research spine: universe, trading calendar, frequency, and the mandatory point-in-time (PIT) policy. A task without an explicit PIT policy is inadmissible at the seam, because without it leakage cannot be ruled out (Q-gate family Q0-Q2). All timestamps are caller-injected; the adapter reads no clock.

task_id.description: Caller-allocated id for the mapped core research-task/v1 record.

study_id.description: Identifier of the study this task belongs to; tasks, claims, evidence, and cases of one study share it.

statement.description: Human-readable task statement, e.g. the factor research question or strategy hypothesis under study.

universe.description: Tradable universe definition (index membership, listing-age filters, suspension handling). A blank universe makes coverage claims uninterpretable and is rejected.

calendar.description: Trading-calendar alignment for the timestamps used in the study (exchange calendar, timezone, alignment convention).

frequency.description: Data and decision frequency of the study (for example daily, minute-bar, event-driven).

pit_policy.description: Mandatory point-in-time discipline statement: which snapshots, revision handling, and availability lags the study commits to. Required and non-blank; an absent PIT policy means leakage cannot be ruled out at the seam.

cost_model.description: Cost and execution assumptions (fees, slippage, impact, fill and position limits). Free-form in v1; the audit obligation lives in the Q3 checkpoint.

data_spec.description: Data requirements of the study (sources, fields, history depth, revision expectations). Free-form in v1.

scope.description: Passed through to the core task draft's scope.

resources.description: Passed through to the core task draft's resources envelope.

created_at.description: Caller-injected freeze timestamp; the adapter never reads a clock.
